messages.content: In one sentence, what makes a network decentralized?

completion: No single machine is in charge: every peer can store, route and serve, so the network keeps working when any one of them leaves.

messages.content: How does a peer find another peer without a central server?

completion: It asks the peers it already knows, which point it closer to the one it wants; a distributed hash table keeps those hops few.

messages.content: What does a relay do when two peers cannot connect directly?

completion: It passes their traffic along: both connect out to the relay, which forwards the bytes, often only until hole punching opens a direct path.

messages.content: Name one trade-off of decentralized networks.

completion: Finding data takes more hops than asking one central server, so lookups are slower.
